elements.element: Customer has no obligation to disclose more favourable third-party commercial offers to Vendor.
elements.evidence: The operative clause states that Customer “is not required to disclose” any more favourable commercial offer it receives.

elements.element: Customer has no obligation to match more favourable third-party commercial offers for Vendor.
elements.evidence: The operative clause states that Customer “is not required to ... match for Vendor” any more favourable commercial offer it receives.

elements.element: If an MFN obligation burdens Customer, it is limited to a specifically defined product.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: the rendered clause expressly imposes no disclosure or matching obligation on Customer, so no MFN applies to any product.

elements.element: If an MFN obligation burdens Customer, its duration does not exceed 12 months.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: the rendered clause imposes no MFN obligation, and therefore none continues beyond 12 months.

elements.element: If an MFN obligation burdens Customer, it applies only to reasonably comparable offers and excludes offers made under materially different circumstances, such as differences in scope, volume, term, geography, service levels, bundling, or promotional terms.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: because Customer has no disclosure or matching obligation, no non-comparable offer can trigger an MFN duty.

result.reason: The operative redline removes both components of the Customer-burdening MFN: disclosure and matching. It therefore fully achieves the preferred position and, a fortiori, stays within all fallback limits. The change is confined to reversing the original obligation and does not add unrelated terms. Drafting is clear, although retaining “Before engaging another provider” is unnecessary once the obligation is negated.
